page: Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 is a storage and memory-dense virtual machine powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor built on x86_64 architecture. Managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. Hardware resources include 32 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB memory ratio per vCPU, 32 MB of L3 cache, and a bundled direct-attached 960 GB NVMe SSD for high-throughput local storage.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-threaded CPU capability, highlighted by high single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores. Multi-core performance, Redis SET operation throughput reaching 5.97 million ops/sec, and static web serving throughput at 6.39 GB/sec perform at average tier levels. Conversely, memory read bandwidth and multi-threaded compilation tasks present lower performance bottlenecks.

By combining an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU allocation with fast local NVMe storage on a dedicated core layout, the L4as_v4 achieves qualitative resource efficiency for memory-conscious and disk IO-heavy operations without requiring dedicated external block storage. This instance configuration is suitable for local database processing, caching clusters, log analytics, and web application backends.
description: Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 is an AMD EPYC 9V74-powered instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs, 32 GB of RAM, and a bundled 960 GB NVMe SSD for fast local storage. Running at 3.7 GHz with AVX-512 instruction support, it demonstrates strong single-core compute performance along with solid throughput in Redis operations (5.97 million ops/sec) and static web serving (6.39 GB/sec). Although memory read bandwidth is lower compared to high-bandwidth compute nodes, its 8 GB per vCPU memory density and integrated NVMe SSD offer an effective resource mix. This instance serves well for local database nodes, in-memory caching layers, search indexing, and web backend deployment.
